pairs.subject: docs-content-model
pairs.evidence: scripts/docs/check-doc-sync.mjs:6 The repo's only docs surface is a directory of markdown files (docs/features/), checked by a docs-sync drift hook. There is no typed topic/category/body catalog, no rendered docs site, and no navigation or draft state, so the subject's precondition (docs modelled as a typed catalog on a product surface) does not hold. A case-insensitive grep of scripts/docs for topic, sidebar, draft, lastReviewed and frontmatter found nothing, and git ls-files shows no docusaurus, mkdocs, vitepress or book.toml docs site in the repo.

techniques.evidence: scripts/docs/feature-doc-map.json:6 Docs are addressed by file path, which is the files-on-disk substrate. Nothing splits a topic record from a body module, so there is no bijection to assert.

scripts/docs/feature-doc-map.json:7 The nearest thing to 'watched sources' is the per-doc sourceGlobs list. It lives in the docs-sync coupling map, which the golden path assigns to the docs-synchronization subject, not on a topic record. There is no review date and no checked-against version anywhere.

pairs.registryProposal: The golden path's seam with docs-synchronization could say what happens on the files-on-disk substrate. There, the 'watched sources' field this subject gives a typed home has no record to live on, and it ends up as globs in the drift gate's coupling map (here: source globs keyed by doc path). A sentence saying whether that counts as the field's legitimate home on that substrate, or as a gap, would stop graders from splitting on it.
